subject: Post-call: function-calling parallelism, auth & routing patterns for PayFlux POC
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Eli Ramirez <eli.ramirez@payflux.com>, Sophie Allen <sophie.allen@payflux.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com, karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: function-calling parallelism, auth & routing patterns for PayFlux POC

Hi Eli / Sophie —

Great conversation earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned before the PoC kickoff: that should make it easier for your engineering team to estimate work.

Summary of requirements we captured:
- Use case: payment dispute triage + automated remediation suggestions. Low-latency first-pass, then async enrichment.
- Must call internal payment tools (transaction DB) and an external sanctions-check service.
- Need structured outputs (JSON) for downstream workflows and strong observability for audit.
- Auth: prefer mTLS for internal toolcalls, API-key for external vendor; SSO for dashboard access.

Architecture options we discussed (high level):
1) Serial function-calling inside the model: model calls tool A (DB), then tool B (sanctions) synchronously. Simpler but higher tail latency.
2) Parallel fanout: send model-generated queries to both tools in parallel, aggregate results with a lightweight reranker/merger. Better latency but requires idempotency and correlation keys.
3) Hybrid: fast cached DB lookup inline, then background enrichment via events and embeddings/reranker for final decision.

Questions we raised for your team:
- Which latency SLO do you need for the first-pass decision? (we heard ~250ms target)
- Are there throttling limits on the sanctions vendor (rate limits)?
- Is storing KV cache acceptable for 30 days in your environment?

Recommended starting design for the PoC (proposed):
- Use SDK-based function calling where Redwood serializes tool definitions (schema-first) and exposes both sync and async invocation.
- For critical lookups (DB), do synchronous calls with a 150ms timeout and local KV cache with 5s refresh TTL for hot keys.
- For external sanctions-check, do parallel invocation with 2s timeout plus fallback to cached verdict (if available). Add exponential backoff for 429s.
- Use a small in-line reranker (embedding-based) to merge parallel results if both return, otherwise accept single result and tag for audit.
- Auth: mTLS between Redwood Private runtime and PayFlux internal tooling; vendor via API key stored in Vault.

Attachments: I’ve attached a short proposal doc (poc-arch-proposal-v1.pdf) and a sample function/schema file (fncall-definitions-sample.json) to illustrate tool definitions and example schemas.

Next steps / asks:
1) Can your infra lead confirm the sanctions vendor rate limits and whether we can do parallel calls?
2) Do you want us to produce a tiny reference implementation (SDK snippets + Docker demo) for the parallel fanout pattern? We can deliver that in the first sprint.
3) Proposed follow-up call Wednesday to align on SLOs and auth gating.

Thanks — Ben

--
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0193

From: Eli Ramirez <eli.ramirez@payflux.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sophie Allen <sophie.allen@payflux.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: function-calling parallelism, auth & routing patterns for PayFlux POC

Ben —

Thanks for the clear recap, very helpful. A few answers and clarifications from our side:

- Latency SLO: for customer-facing triage we’re hoping to stay under ~300ms  p95 for the first-pass. If hybrid delivers sub-300ms p95 we’re happy.
- Sanctions vendor: our contract limits are 500 reqs/minute and the vendor has 1s median latency, occasional 2–3s tails. They return 429 with a 60s Retry-After header when throttled.
- KV cache: storing derived verdicts for 30 days is acceptable for the PoC; PII policy will be enforced (no raw card numbers).

We like the proposed hybrid approach: inline DB fast-path + parallel sanctions vendor + embedding rerank for merges. A couple of asks:
1) Can you include guidance on correlation IDs and idempotency tokens for parallel calls? We need to ensure retries won’t create duplicate remediation actions.
2) For auditability, can you recommend an event schema that includes model prompt hash, tool inputs, tool outputs, and final decision rationale?

We’re ok with a reference SDK demo. Wednesday works — 10am PT.

Thanks — Eli

--
Eli Ramirez
Head of Platform Engineering, PayFlux
eli.ramirez@payflux.com

From: laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Eli Ramirez <eli.ramirez@payflux.com>, Sophie Allen <sophie.allen@payflux.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 15:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: function-calling parallelism, auth & routing patterns for PayFlux POC

Eli / Team —

Good context — thanks. I pulled together a concise implementation pattern and attached three artifacts:
- poc-arch-proposal-v1.pdf: end-to-end sequence, SLO knobs, and fallback policy decision table.
- fncall-definitions-sample.json: example of our schema-first tool definitions (name, inputs, outputs, error codes).
- auth-routing-matrix.xlsx: mapping for mTLS vs API-key vs user SSO and recommended routing.

Key technical notes (high level):
- Correlation & idempotency: use a 128-bit request_id generated at the API gateway; pass it as request_id across all tool invocations. For retries, include an idempotency_token derived from (request_id, tool_name, timestamp-window). Store idempotency cache for 30s for fast-path ops and 24h for system-initiated remediations.
- Parallel fanout pattern: Redwood runtime will fanout to defined tool endpoints in parallel and return as soon as a quorum rule is satisfied. For PoC we recommend quorum=1 with reranker score threshold guard (i.e., accept first result if confidence > 0.85 otherwise wait for second result).
- Error handling: classify errors into transient (5xx, 429), permanent (4xx invalid input), and business (e.g., sanction hit). For transient errors implement jittered exponential backoff (base=100ms, max=2s, max retries=3). For 429 prefer honor Retry-After and use circuit-breaker until healthy.
- Reranker: use embedding-based similarity (batch embeddings for candidate tool outputs + small transformer reranker). Keep reranker model small (100M) to run inline in Redwood Dedicated for latency reasons.
- Structured output: we’ll enforce JSON Schema for tool outputs and a stable envelope: {"request_id","tool_name","status","payload","meta":{"latency_ms","source"}}.

I attached sample code snippets in the PDF and JSON for the function definitions. If PayFlux wants, we can scope a 1-week spike: SDK + Docker demo that shows parallel fanout, idempotency, and a simple reranker. Estimate: 3 engineer-days + 1 architect review.

Ben / Karthik — can you confirm the spike estimate and whether we build on Redwood Hosted test environment or set up a short-lived Dedicated node in AWS us-west-2 for latency validation?

Laura

--
Laura Bennett
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com | +1 650-555-0118

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Eli Ramirez <eli.ramirez@payflux.com>, Sophie Allen <sophie.allen@payflux.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com, karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 11:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: function-calling parallelism, auth & routing patterns for PayFlux POC

Thanks Eli — great answers.

Confirming next steps:
- PayFlux infra to confirm vendor rate limits and whether we can request a higher quota during the PoC (Eli).
- Redwood to spin up a 1-week spike: SDK snippets + Docker demo + small Dedicated node in us-west-2 for latency checks (Laura / Karthik).
- Spike estimate: 3 eng-days + 1 architect review; target deliverable by next Wednesday EOD.
- Meeting: Wed 10am PT (I’ll send invite).

We’ll include the correlation/idempotency pattern and the JSON event envelope in the demo. Also we’ll wire in a simple embedding-based reranker as a standalone container so your team can measure p95 impact and tune quorum/confidence thresholds.

If that all sounds good I’ll create the HubSpot task and attach the PoC materials to the deal.

Ben

--
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
